channel.title: DVIDIA Research
channel.description: Research footprints on demonstrations, calibrated simulation and robot skills.

item.title: PiPER grip validation and recovery
item.description: Moderate-friction regression · baseline 4/6, guarded 2/6 · hardware unqualified. A slow test lift and bounded supported retry add recorded acquisition decisions to the pinned PiPER contact pilot, but completion regresses: at moderate friction baseline completes 2/2 and guarded completes 0/2. Both complete 2/2 normal cases; neither completes the two low-friction cases. All 30 attempts remain numerically valid, including 18 failed controls and full-duration aborts. Four qualification decisions are followed by a brief independent following window, yet two tasks still fail; no successful recovery or overall improvement is demonstrated. Actual motion continues after hold requests, and 53/30,000 computation windows exceed 20 ms. Complete compressed receipts, original model notices and pinned offline inspection preserve the evidence. Authored privileged-state simulation establishes no detector accuracy, learned shoe skill, calibrated contact or physical robot qualification.

item.title: Native grasp task benchmark
item.description: 6/6 simulated placements · controls 0/12 · real-time and hardware unqualified. A pinned six-axis arm and coupled gripper complete 6/6 frozen synthetic rigid-block placements, while matched recorded-arm/open-jaw and hold controls complete 0/12. Native contact must produce grasp, sustained lift, retained carry, release and settled placement with tool retreat. All 18 attempts and timing traces remain in the receipt; one placement takes 29.51 wall seconds for 20 simulated seconds and misses 251 of 1,000 computation windows, so real-time operation is not established. An offline 3D mesh replay exposes the recorded motion. The authored privileged-state baseline provides a benchmark for a future compact DVIDIA action policy, not a learned footage-to-action model, validated shoe simulation or physical robot qualification.

item.title: Hardware matched robot simulation
item.description: Pinned CPU mechanics · PiPER contact pilot · physical fidelity unmeasured. A separate UR5e/Robotiq reference preserves pinned geometry, inertias, moving-link collision proxies and coupled gripper structure: fourteen modeled coordinates and seven commands. Eighteen deterministic unloaded motion/closure runs are numerically valid; at a 1 ms step, CPU physics throughput measures 40.80–47.29 simulated seconds per measured stepping wall second on one host, excluding loading, sensing, rendering, policy and real actuation. Adjacent timestep comparisons and a matched static overlap expose numerical sensitivity and collision participation. A pure-Python paired trace scorer measures joint, tool and jaw mismatch without automatic qualification. Left/right five-finger references are separately audited; LeRobot collection with an original DVIDIA policy is proposed. Serial calibration, physical response, shoe task learning and bimanual execution remain unmeasured. An offline 3D mesh replay now exposes the recorded arm/gripper poses without rerunning physics. PiPER and SO-101 now have pinned CPU profiles with 6/6 valid unloaded numerical attempts each and explicit native command units. PiPER also has a frozen authored rigid-block contact pilot: nominal placement 2/2, low-friction placement 0/1, open-jaw 0/3 and hold 0/3, with all nine attempts numerically valid. One of 9,000 computation windows exceeds 20 ms; hardware real-time response is unqualified. SO-101 object tasks, learned policies and physical qualification remain open. YAM, OpenArm, ARX X5 and PAROL6 remain upcoming.

item.title: DVIDIA Observation Lab pilot
item.description: Local review release · motion and actuator source pilots · hardware unqualified. DVIDIA Observation Lab supplies local object/palm proposals, reviewed timeline revisions and separate causal image-motion forecasts; real annotation and motion accuracy remain unmeasured. A new CPU pilot learns next-20-ms joint/jaw deltas from current native state and issued commands. Twelve seeded groups retain 36 recordings with 8/2/2 train/development/test grouping; 4,553 test transitions are not independent robot trials. The 6,438-byte action model computes at 0.207 ms p95 on one host and improves RMSE, while jaw MAE/worst error regress against persistence and an initial opening is substantially overpredicted. These are privileged simulator measurements and model-only timings. A proposed shoe capture plan has no footage or executed shoe benchmark. The v0.1 release and hosted synthetic review demo remain separate; no shoe policy, physical adapter, validated shoe physics or hardware qualification is established.

item.title: Robotics research pipeline
item.description: Architecture proposal · current simulation alpha · hardware unqualified. An updated architecture connects immutable Skillspace recordings, reviewed task-label proposals and synchronized measured telemetry to grouped datasets, separate visual and motor learners, and a proposed local state supervisor. The implemented CPU baseline retains authored phases, gripper decisions and recovery around its learned joint-delta head. New annotation and supervisor pilots, fresh frozen confirmation, physics calibration and compatible skill-installation gates define the next milestones. Automatic labeling, learned supervision, human-video action recovery and physical arm qualification remain unestablished; this publication adds no new training or hardware result.

item.title: Skillspace footage training pipeline
item.description: Public CPU package · one native scene qualified · simulation-only. The public Dvidia-Inference/dvidia-training repository provides a standalone CPU pipeline that audits Skillspace media, freezes grouped splits and exports inspectable artifacts. Ten synthetic six-second clips train a visual predictor with a 0.5106-second median pipeline time across three repeats on one macOS host. Aligned native simulator telemetry supplies 4,029 training labels for a learned joint-delta head, evaluated on one held-out recording. Its capsule passes native placement qualification in that recording's exact scene; identical joint targets with open jaws fail. Installation and hardware guides accompany the package. Human-video action recovery, shoe organization, demonstration sufficiency, independent scene generalization and physical robot competence remain unestablished.

item.title: Skill capsule acquisition and optimization
item.description: Simulation-only · teacher/student 7/8 · no overall speedup. A compact learned CPU movement head replaces joint-target computation inside an authored placement supervisor. Teacher and student both pass 7/8 in a new frozen evaluation, while episode wall time increases from 6.273 to 6.360 seconds. A 39,845-byte JSON capsule imports into the local lab, checks its exact runtime and qualifies the current scene through native placement and a recorded-arm/open-jaw control. Scene changes require a fresh test. One known scene and repeat pass native network denial; perception, complete task learning, other embodiments and hardware remain unqualified.

item.title: Skillspace arm benchmarks and evolution
item.description: Mixed held-out result · 30/32 baseline, 29/32 updated. Two controller revisions improve development completion from 14/20 to 17/20, but the frozen paired test declines from 30/32 to 29/32: both pass all 24 normal-strength cases while actuator-stress completion falls from 6/8 to 5/8. Instrumented CPU throughput also declines. We publish the regression, unchanged contact and success rules, exact controller snapshots, richer physical inputs, runtime-bound installation and a proposed staged Skillspace contract. Contact forces and penetration remain uncalibrated; learned perception and physical qualification are open.

item.title: Installing a Skillspace on a simulated arm
item.description: Public skill link to authored adapter · 6/6 scene placements. The first link-to-arm product path installs an existing DVIDIA placement envelope, binds a local authored controller to one simulated arm, and reuses it in independently grounded scenes. Native jaw contacts carry a free box; six layouts complete, while no-motion and identical joint commands with open jaws each complete zero of six. Installed execution passes process-level offline checks. Task metadata contains no learned policy; perception, cup geometry, full arm collisions and physical qualification remain open.

item.title: Offline cable training environment
item.description: CPU simulation-only · Controller search and frozen evaluation executed. The first runnable product loop combines an anchored cable environment, local controller-parameter search, frozen evaluation, offline replay and a manifest-backed skill pack. The selected controller and a fixed feedback baseline both completed 10/10 held-out simulated episodes; zero-force and release controls completed 0/10. A native macOS network-denial run completed 3/3 additional episodes. Ideal endpoint attachment and privileged state bound the result; physical rope calibration, gripping, sensors and GPU throughput remain untested.

item.title: Fast accurate robot training simulation
item.description: 54 CPU fixture trials · GPU and physical transfer untested. A design for an offline, self-hosted training environment that turns demonstrations into calibrated practice and qualified robot skills. We examine contact, deformation, sensor feedback and the performance–accuracy tradeoff, then report 54 deterministic native MuJoCo CPU fixture trials. Fine endpoint agreement did not establish accurate contact transients, and coarse timesteps missed collisions. Minimum GPU memory, rope accuracy and physical transfer remain unmeasured.

item.title: Grok robotics research on X
item.description: Primary sources checked · Experiments proposed. Three Grok 4.7 research passes surface observation-to-action, synthetic-practice and reusable-repair ideas. Independent primary-source checks compare those findings with our thesis: observation supplies goals and state, language retrieves a skill, spatial expectations guide attention, and executable feedback with evaluation establishes competence. X posts remain discovery leads. No universal demonstration count or arbitrary-robot transfer follows from the reviewed results.

item.title: Spatially grounded downloadable robot skills
item.description: Source review · DVIDIA experiments not run. A synthesis of learning from human demonstrations, language-conditioned spatial attention, simulation expansion and robot-specific skill delivery. Spatial priors can accelerate inspection but do not determine contact state or control. The proposed downloadable skill packages a controller, initiation and termination conditions, compatible sensing and hardware, recovery behavior and measured evidence. Separate experiments would test attention, data coverage, feedback and transfer.

item.title: Clef and grounded video observations
item.description: Five licensed excerpts · Accuracy evaluation outstanding. A preregistered image-API feasibility run processed five licensed three-second POV excerpts using four timestamped frames, a Gemma caption and a Clef-flash check. All five completed at a price-derived inference estimate of $0.00140634. Post-run inspection found an object error accepted by the checker and omitted state changes. API and schema compatibility were demonstrated; annotation accuracy and whole-task success were not.

item.title: From Skillspace to robot skill
item.description: Graduation and robot training not run. An Argus review and a proposal to connect original recordings, reviewed episodes, immutable datasets, training runs, held-out evaluation and robot-tested releases. The review separates video annotation from action supervision and defines compatibility beyond a robot’s degree-of-freedom count. A proposed 40-episode annotation pilot and evidence-based graduation criteria remain unrun.

item.title: Turn physical footage into testable evidence
item.description: Four baseline protocols proposed. A research agenda covering visible capture evidence, relations over time, evaluation provenance and physical grounding. Each question has a bounded protocol and a failure condition. The aim is to measure whether structure and physical signals improve a defined task before scaling collection. Strategic opinions, author-reported results and our untested proposals are kept distinct.
